passages.text: Make contentment thine earrings, modesty and self-respect thy wallet, meditation the ashes to smear on thy body. Make thy body, which is only a morsel for death, thy beggar’s coat, and faith thy rule of life and thy staff.
passages.note: Inner virtues as the true spiritual discipline

passages.text: I have no strength to speak and no strength to be silent. T have no strength to ask and no strength to give; I have no strength to live and no strength to die; I have no strength to acquire empire or wealth, which produce 2 commotion in the heart. T have no strength to meditate on Thee or ponder on divine knowledge; T have no strength to find the way to escape from the world. He in whose arm there is strength may see what he can do. Nanak, no one is of superior or inferior strength before God.
passages.note: Feeling powerless; humility before something greater

passages.text: Make continence Thy furnace, forbearance Thy goldsmith, Understanding Thine anvil, divine knowledge Thy tools, The fear of God Thy bellows, austerities Thy fire, Divine love Thy crucible, and melt God’s name therein. In such a true mint the Word shall be coined.
passages.note: Shaping character through patient spiritual practice

passages.text: The air is the Guru, water our father, and the great earth our mother; Day and night are our two nurses, male and female, who set the whole world a-playing. Merits and demerits shall be read out in the presence of the judge. According to men’s acts, some shall be near and others distant from God. Those who have pondered on the name and departed after the completion of their toil, Shall have their countenances made bright, O Nanak; how many shall be emancipated in company with them!
passages.note: Belonging to nature; actions shape our closeness to God
